props.gloss_en: the mishna: a person may draw lots with his sons and his household at the table [on Shabbat]
the mishna: provided he does not intend to make a large portion against a small one
Shmuel: members of a group who are particular with one another transgress [the prohibitions of] measure, weight and number, and of borrowing and repaying on a festival
Shmuel: and according to Beit Hillel, [they transgress] also on account of interest
Rav: it is permitted to lend to one's sons and household with interest, to give them a taste of interest
Rav: the purpose is to give them a taste of interest
the mishna is defective and teaches thus [the three clauses that follow]
reconstructed: a person may draw lots with his sons and household at the table, even a large portion against a small one
reconstructed: with his sons and household, yes; with others, no

the reason: on account of dice-gaming
